\[
d(x,y) = \max_{c} \bigl| I_c(x,y) - m_c(x,y) \bigr|,
\qquad
I_{\text{out},c}(x,y) =
\begin{cases}
m_c(x,y) & d(x,y) > T \\
I_c(x,y) & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(m_c(x, y)\): Median of channel c over the neighbors of (x, y)
- \(d(x, y)\): The largest channel difference to the neighbor median
- \(T\): The threshold

m_c is the median of channel c over the neighbors, the window without the pixel itself. The pixel is left out, so a defect cannot pull its own reference. The neighbor count is even, so the median is the mean of the two middle values. A pixel whose largest channel difference d is above T is defective, and all its channels get the neighbor medians.
